chapter.name: Union and Its Territory
chapter.blurb: Articles 1 to 4, reorganisation of states, evolution of states and union territories.

concepts.name: Union of States and the territory of India (Articles 1 and 2)

questions.q: According to Ambedkar, the phrase 'Union of States' was preferred to 'Federation of States' because the Indian Federation
questions.a: is not the result of an agreement among the states, and the states have no right to secede from it
o: is not the result of an agreement among the states, and the states have no right to secede from it
is the result of an agreement among the states, as in the American Federation, but they may not secede from it
is not the result of an agreement among the states, but a state may secede with the consent of Parliament
is the result of an agreement among the states and may be dissolved by a two-thirds vote of the state legislatures
questions.e: Ambedkar gave two reasons - the federation is not the result of an agreement among the states like the American Federation, and the states have no right to secede.
w: It keeps the right reason about agreement but reverses the American-style agreement; the Indian federation is not an agreement.
It drops the second reason: the states have no right to secede at all, not even with Parliament's consent.
It reverses both reasons: there was no agreement among states and no right to dissolve the Union.

questions.q: Which one of the following is included in the 'Territory of India' but is NOT included in the 'Union of India'?
o: Tribal areas within a state, covered by the Sixth Schedule
Scheduled areas within a state, covered by the Fifth Schedule
questions.e: The Union of India includes only the states, while the Territory of India also includes union territories and territories that may be acquired. Fifth and Sixth Schedule areas lie within the states.
w: Sixth Schedule tribal areas are within the states, so they already belong to the Union of India.
Fifth Schedule scheduled areas are within the states, so they are part of the Union of India.
The territories of the states are exactly what the Union of India consists of.

questions.q: The special provisions in Part XXI of the Constitution applicable to Maharashtra, Gujarat, Nagaland and certain other states
questions.a: override the general provisions relating to the states as a class
o: override the general provisions relating to the states as a class
are overridden by the general provisions relating to the states as a class
apply in addition to, and never prevail over, the general provisions on the states
are confined to the scheduled areas and tribal areas of those states under the Fifth and Sixth Schedules
questions.e: Although the provisions pertaining to states apply to all in the same manner, the Part XXI special provisions override the general provisions. The Fifth and Sixth Schedules are a separate arrangement for scheduled and tribal areas.
w: It reverses the hierarchy: Part XXI prevails over the general provisions.
'Never prevail' is wrong: the Part XXI provisions override the general provisions.
It confuses Part XXI with the Fifth and Sixth Schedules, which are a distinct set of provisions.

questions.q: India's acquisition of Puducherry, Goa, Daman and Diu and Dadra and Nagar Haveli since the commencement of the Constitution illustrates that India, as a sovereign state, can
questions.a: acquire foreign territories by the modes recognised in international law
o: acquire foreign territories by the modes recognised in international law
acquire foreign territory only through a constitutional amendment under Article 368
acquire foreign territory only by admitting it as a state under Article 2
acquire foreign territory only with the consent of the state legislatures concerned
questions.e: A sovereign state may acquire foreign territory by cession, occupation, conquest or subjugation, and India's acquisition of these territories is an example.
w: Nothing in the passage ties acquisition itself to Article 368; the Court's amendment requirement concerns ceding Indian territory away.
Article 2 deals with admitting or establishing states; acquired territories are a separate category under Article 1.
State legislatures have no role in acquiring foreign territory.

questions.q: Among the modes by which a sovereign state acquires foreign territory under international law, the one applied to territory hitherto unoccupied by a recognised ruler is
questions.e: Cession follows treaty, purchase, gift, lease or plebiscite; occupation applies to territory hitherto unoccupied by a recognised ruler; then conquest or subjugation.
w: Cession is a transfer by treaty, purchase, gift, lease or plebiscite.
Conquest is acquisition by force of arms, not of unoccupied land.
Subjugation is acquisition by overpowering an existing ruler.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 1 of the Constitution:

1. The Constituent Assembly was not unanimous on the name of the country and adopted a mix of both names, 'India, that is, Bharat'.
2. Article 1 deals with the name of the country and the procedure for admitting new states.
3. The phrase 'Union of States' was preferred to 'Federation of States' because the Indian Federation resulted from an agreement among the states.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 1 deals with two things, the name of the country and the type of polity; admission of new states comes under Article 2. Statement 3 is incorrect: according to Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, the Indian Federation is not the result of an agreement among the states, unlike the American Federation.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect:
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the 'Union of India' and the 'Territory of India':

1. Union territories are members of the federal system and share a distribution of powers with the Centre.
2. The 'Union of India' includes only the states.
3. The 'Territory of India' is a wider expression than the 'Union of India'.
4. Territories that may be acquired by India are directly administered by the Central government.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the states are the members of the federal system; union territories are directly administered by the Centre. Statement 2 is correct: the Union includes only states, the Territory also includes union territories and acquired territories. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is correct.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 1, which is incorrect:
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the states covered by the special provisions of Part XXI:

1. Telangana is among the states to which the Part XXI special provisions apply.
2. Mizoram and Arunachal Pradesh are among the states to which the Part XXI special provisions apply.
3. Goa and Karnataka are among the states to which the Part XXI special provisions apply.
4. Sikkim and Nagaland are among the states to which the Part XXI special provisions apply.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

w: '1, 3 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 4, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct.

1. Article 2 gives Parliament only the power to establish new states, and no power to admit states that already exist.
2. Article 3, unlike Article 2, deals with the formation of or changes in the existing states of the Union.
3. New states under Article 2 are admitted or established on such terms and conditions as Parliament thinks fit.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Article 2 grants two powers, to admit existing states and to establish new ones. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct:
'2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

2. The country is an integral whole, divided into different states only for the convenience of administration.
3. The federation is called a Union because it is indestructible.

questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: Ambedkar said the Indian Federation is not the result of an agreement among the states. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the territories acquired by India:

1. Puducherry was handed over to India by the Portuguese in 1954.
2. Goa, Daman and Diu were acquired from the Portuguese by means of a police action in 1961.
3. Acquired territories, like states, share a distribution of powers with the Centre.
4. India may acquire foreign territory by cession, occupation, conquest or subjugation.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the French handed Puducherry over in 1954; it was administered as an 'acquired territory' till it was made a union territory in 1962. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: they are directly administered by the Central government. Statement 4 is correct.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about modes of acquiring foreign territory:

1. Transfer of territory by purchase, gift, lease or plebiscite is a separate mode and not a form of cession.
2. Occupation refers to acquiring territory already ruled by a recognised ruler.
3. Conquest and subjugation are also modes recognised by international law.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: cession itself covers treaty, purchase, gift, lease or plebiscite. Statement 2 is incorrect: occupation relates to territory hitherto unoccupied by a recognised ruler. Statement 3 is correct.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 1 and the Fifth and Sixth Schedules:

1. The Fifth and Sixth Schedules contain provisions for the administration of the union territories.
2. The special provisions of Part XXI apply, among others, to Sikkim, Goa and Karnataka.
3. The names of the states and union territories are mentioned in the Second Schedule.
4. The Naga Hills-Tuensang Area of Assam was a tribal area specified in the Fifth Schedule.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: they apply to scheduled areas and tribal areas within the states. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is incorrect: they are mentioned in the First Schedule. Statement 4 is incorrect: it was a tribal area specified in the Sixth Schedule, not the Fifth.
w: '3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'2 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the territory of India after the Jammu and Kashmir Reorganisation Act, 2019:

1. The names of the states and union territories are mentioned in the First Schedule of the Constitution.
2. The number of states and union territories rose from 14 and 6 in 1956 to 28 and 8 respectively.
3. India has 29 states and 7 union territories, 29 being the ordinal of Telangana, the latest state to be created.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the First Schedule lists the names of the States and Union Territories (Articles 1 and 4). Statement 2 is correct: the number of states and union territories rose from 14 and 6 in 1956 to 28 and 8 respectively. Statement 3 is incorrect: the position is 28 states and 8 union territories. The 29th is only Telangana's creation ordinal; the state count fell to 28 when Jammu and Kashmir became a union territory in 2019.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect (the state count is 28, not 29) and leaves out statement 2, which is correct (14 states and 6 UTs in 1956 rose to 28 and 8).
'2 and 3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect (the state count is 28, not 29) and leaves out statement 1, which is correct (the First Schedule names the States and UTs).
'2 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: the First Schedule names the States and Union Territories.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the categories of the territory of India under Article 1:

1. Territories of the states form one category.
2. Territories of the princely states form a separate category.
3. Union territories form one category.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the three categories are states, union territories and territories that may be acquired. Statement 3 is correct. So exactly 2 are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 3).
'All three' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 3).
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 2 are correct (statements 1, 3).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 1 and the federation:

1. Article 1 describes India as a 'Federation of States'.
2. The states have a right to secede from the Indian Union.
3. The Constituent Assembly was unanimous on the name of the country.
4. Territories that may be acquired by India are outside the scope of Article 1.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it describes India as a 'Union of States'. Statement 2 is incorrect: they have no right to secede. Statement 3 is incorrect: there was no unanimity; it adopted a mix, 'India, that is, Bharat'. Statement 4 is incorrect: they are the third category of the territory of India. So exactly 0 are correct.
w: 'Only three' miscounts: exactly 0 are correct.
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 0 are correct.
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 0 are correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Articles 2 and 3:

1. Article 2 relates to the admission or establishment of new states that are not part of the Union of India.
2. Article 3 relates to the formation of or changes in the existing states of the Union.
3. Article 3 deals with the internal re-adjustment inter se of the territories of the constituent states.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct. So exactly 3 are correct.
w: 'None' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: Union territories and acquired territories are directly administered by the Central government.
Statement-II: Union territories and acquired territories are the members of the federal system.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
o: Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct: union territories and acquired territories are administered directly by the Central government (Article 239). Statement-II is incorrect: only the states are members of the federal system and share powers with the Centre. The first holds; the second wrongly gives the states' status to the other categories.
w: Rejected: Statement-II is incorrect, so no reading in which both are correct can hold.
Rejected: Statement-II is incorrect, so no reading in which both are correct can hold.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct (the Centre administers these territories directly), so it cannot be called incorrect.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements:

Statement-I: The Constituent Assembly adopted 'India, that is, Bharat' as the name of the country.
Statement-II: There was no unanimity in the Constituent Assembly on whether the traditional or the modern name should be used.

Which one of the following is correct in respect of the above statements?
questions.a: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
o: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct and Statement-II explains Statement-I
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct but Statement-II does not explain Statement-I
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct
questions.e: Statement-I is correct. Statement-II is correct. The lack of agreement is the reason the Assembly settled on a mix of both names.
w: Rejected: Statement-II does give the reason: disagreement forced the compromise of using both names.
Rejected: Statement-II is correct, not incorrect.
Rejected: Statement-I is correct, not incorrect.

questions.q:
Match the provision in List-I with its subject in List-II.

List-I
A. Article 1
B. Article 2
C. First Schedule
D. Part XXI special provisions

List-II
1. Override the general provisions relating to certain listed states
2. Name of the country and the type of polity
3. Names of the states and union territories and their territorial extent
4. Admission or establishment of new states not part of the Union
questions.e: Article 1 - name and polity; First Schedule - names and extent; Part XXI - special provisions overriding general ones.: Article 2 - admission or establishment of new states.
w: A and B are interchanged: Article 1 names the country, Article 2 admits new states.
C and D are interchanged: the First Schedule lists the states; Part XXI holds special provisions.
A and C are interchanged: Article 1 deals with name and polity, the Schedule with the lists.

concepts.name: Parliament's power to reorganise states (Articles 3 and 4) and the Berubari case

questions.q: Because Article 4 says that laws made under Articles 2 and 3 are not to be considered amendments of the Constitution under Article 368, a bill altering the name of a state can be passed by
questions.a: a simple majority in the ordinary legislative process
o: a simple majority in the ordinary legislative process
a special majority of each House of Parliament, without any ratification
a special majority of Parliament and ratification by half of the state legislatures
a simple majority of Parliament, followed by a two-thirds majority of the state legislature concerned
questions.e: Such laws can be passed by a simple majority and by the ordinary legislative process.
w: A special majority is the Article 368 route, which Article 4 takes these laws out of.
Ratification by states is a feature of Article 368 amendments of federal provisions, not of these laws.
The state legislature only gives its views; it does not vote the bill through by any majority.

questions.q: In the Berubari Union reference (1960), the Supreme Court held that Parliament's power under Article 3 to diminish the area of a state
questions.a: does not cover cession of Indian territory to a foreign country
o: does not cover cession of Indian territory to a foreign country
includes cession of Indian territory to a foreign country by an ordinary law
includes cession of territory to a foreign country only if the state legislature concerned consents
is limited to altering the names of the states and cannot reduce their area
questions.e: The Court held Article 3 does not cover cession to a foreign country; this needs an amendment under Article 368, hence the 9th Amendment.
w: That is the opposite of the holding.
The Court did not make the cession turn on the state legislature's consent; it required an Article 368 amendment.
Article 3 expressly lets Parliament diminish the area of any state.

questions.q: The Supreme Court ruled in 1969 that the settlement of a boundary dispute between India and another country
questions.a: can be done by executive action, as no territory is ceded
o: can be done by executive action, as no territory is ceded
requires an amendment of the Constitution under Article 368
requires a law of Parliament under Article 3 with the views of the state concerned
can be done only after a presidential reference to the Supreme Court
questions.e: A boundary settlement does not need an amendment; it can be done by executive action as it does not involve cession of territory.
w: That is the rule for ceding territory (Berubari), not for settling a boundary.
Article 3 deals with internal reorganisation, not settlement with another country.
A reference was used in the Berubari matter, but the 1969 ruling does not require one.

questions.q: When Parliament acts under Article 3 in respect of a union territory, the Constitution requires that
questions.a: no reference need be made to the legislature of the union territory to ascertain its views
o: no reference need be made to the legislature of the union territory to ascertain its views
the President must refer the bill to the union territory's legislature, whose views bind Parliament
the legislature of the union territory must pass a resolution of consent
the legislature of the neighbouring state must be consulted instead
questions.e: In case of a union territory no reference need be made to the concerned legislature and Parliament can act as it deems fit.
w: The reference is a condition for states, and even there the views are not binding.
Even for states, consent is not required; for union territories no reference is needed.
The Constitution makes no provision for consulting a neighbouring state's legislature.

questions.q: The USA is described as 'an indestructible union of indestructible states' because there
questions.a: the federal government cannot alter state borders without the states' consent
o: the federal government cannot alter state borders without the states' consent
the states may leave the union by a resolution of their legislatures
the federal government may alter the borders of states by an ordinary law of the Congress
the territorial integrity of states is protected only against changes of their names
questions.e: The continued existence of a state is guaranteed by the American Constitution; the federal government cannot alter states without consent.
w: American states have no right to leave; the Union is described as indestructible.
That describes India, where Parliament can alter states without consent.
The guarantee covers continued existence and borders, not only names.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the powers of Parliament under Article 3:

1. Parliament can form a new state by separating territory from any state.
2. Parliament can form a new state by uniting two or more states or parts of states, or by uniting any territory to a part of a state.
3. Parliament can alter the name of any state.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct.
w: '1 and 2 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'2 and 3 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the conditions for an Article 3 bill:

1. Before recommending the bill, the President has to refer it to the state legislature concerned for its views within a specified period.
2. The bill can be introduced in Parliament only with the prior recommendation of the Governor of the state concerned.
3. The President is not bound by the views of the state legislature even if they are received in time.
4. The reference to the state legislature must be made after the bill has been passed by Parliament.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: the prior recommendation required is that of the President, not the Governor. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is incorrect: the President refers the bill to the state legislature before recommending it.
w: '3 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct:
'1 and 4 only' includes statement 4, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Berubari reference:

1. The reference arose from the Centre's decision to cede part of Berubari Union (West Bengal) to Bangladesh.
2. The Court held that Parliament's power to diminish a state's area under Article 3 does not cover cession to a foreign country.
3. The 9th Constitutional Amendment Act (1960) was enacted to transfer the Berubari territory to Pakistan.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: the territory was to be ceded to Pakistan. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct.
w: '1 and 2 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements comparing India and the USA:

1. In India the territorial integrity of a state is guaranteed by the Constitution.
2. The Union Government can destroy the states, whereas the state governments cannot destroy the Union.
3. In the USA the continued existence of a state is guaranteed by the Constitution.
4. The Indian Constitution authorises Parliament to alter the areas, boundaries or names of states without their consent.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it is not guaranteed; India is an indestructible union of destructible states. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is correct.
w: '1, 2 and 4 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 3, which is correct:
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 4, which is correct:
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 3, which is correct:

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about Article 4:

1. Article 4 declares that laws made under Articles 2 and 3 are not amendments of the Constitution under Article 368.
2. Laws under Articles 2 and 3 become amendments under Article 368 only when they change the name of a state.
3. Laws made under Articles 2 and 3 cannot provide for amendment of the First and Fourth Schedules.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is incorrect: no such law is treated as an amendment under Article 368. Statement 3 is incorrect: Article 4 lets such laws provide for amendment of the First and Fourth Schedules.
w: '2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1 and 2 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect.
'3 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the constitutional provisions on the territory of the Union:

1. Article 2A, which made Sikkim an associate state, has been repealed.
2. Article 1 deals with the formation of new states and the alteration of areas, boundaries or names of existing states.
3. Article 4 allows laws under Articles 2 and 3 to provide for amendment of the First and Fourth Schedules.
4. Article 2 deals with the admission or establishment of new states.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: Article 2A, inserted when Sikkim became an associate state (35th Amendment, 1974), was repealed by the 36th Amendment (1975) when Sikkim became a full state. Statement 2 is incorrect: Article 1 deals with the name and territory of the Union; formation of states and alteration of areas, boundaries or names is under Article 3. Statement 3 is correct: Article 4 says such laws are not to be treated as amendments under Article 368. Statement 4 is correct: Article 2 empowers Parliament to admit into the Union, or establish, new states; Article 3 deals with changes in existing states.
w: '1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect (Article 1 names the Union and its territory, not changes to states) and leaves out statement 4, which is correct (Article 2 admits or establishes new states).
'1, 2, 3 and 4' includes statement 2, which is incorrect: Article 1 deals with the name and territory of the Union; the alteration of states is Article 3.
'2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 2, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 1, which is correct: Article 2A (Sikkim as associate state) was repealed by the 36th Amendment.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the formation of states and union territories under Article 3:

1. The power to form new states includes the power to form a new state or union territory by uniting a part of any state or union territory to another state or union territory.
2. The 18th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1966 added the wording described in statement 1.
3. The 18th Constitutional Amendment Act of 1966 removed the requirement of the President's prior recommendation for Article 3 bills.
4. For a union territory, no reference need be made to its legislature before Parliament acts.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the explanation to Article 3 says the power to form new states includes uniting a part of any state or union territory to another state or union territory. Statement 2 is correct: this wording was added by the 18th Amendment Act of 1966. Statement 3 is incorrect: that amendment only added the wording on uniting a part of a state or union territory to another; the condition of the President's prior recommendation under Article 3 remains. Statement 4 is correct: the proviso requiring a reference to the legislature for its views applies to states only, so none is needed for a union territory.
w: '2, 3 and 4 only' includes statement 3, which is incorrect (the President's recommendation is still required) and leaves out statement 1, which is correct.
'1 and 4 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct: the 18th Amendment (1966) added the wording on uniting parts of states or UTs.
'2 and 4 only' leaves out statement 1, which is correct: Article 3 covers uniting a part of a state or UT to another.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about laws made under Article 3:

1. The Andhra State Act (1953) formed the State of Andhra by uniting the Telugu-speaking areas of Hyderabad with Madras.
2. The Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur (New State) Act (1954) formed the new state of Himachal Pradesh by uniting the existing states of Himachal Pradesh and Bilaspur.
3. The Chandernagore (Merger) Act (1954) merged the former French enclave of Chandernagore into West Bengal.

Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is incorrect: it took the Telugu-speaking areas out of the Madras State. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct.
w: '1 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect and leaves out statement 2, which is correct.
'1, 2 and 3 only' includes statement 1, which is incorrect.
'3 only' leaves out statement 2, which is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about laws made under Article 3:

1. The Bihar and West Bengal (Transfer of Territories) Act (1956) provided for transfer of certain territories from Bihar to West Bengal.
2. The Rajasthan and Madhya Pradesh (Transfer of Territories) Act (1959) provided for transfer of certain territories from Rajasthan to Madhya Pradesh.
3. The Acquired Territories (Merger) Act (1960) merged into Assam, Punjab and West Bengal certain territories acquired from Pakistan under the 1958 and 1959 agreements.
4. The Andhra Pradesh and Mysore (Transfer of Territory) Act (1968) provided for transfer of certain territory from Andhra Pradesh to Mysore.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct. Statement 2 is correct. Statement 3 is correct. Statement 4 is incorrect: the transfer was from Mysore to Andhra Pradesh. So exactly 3 are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'All four' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Article 3 procedure and powers:

1. Before recommending an Article 3 bill that merely renames a state, the President need not refer it to the state legislature.
2. Parliament cannot, under Article 3, unite a part of a state with a union territory.

4. Parliament may form a new state by uniting two or more states or parts of states.

Statement 4 is correct: Article 3 lets Parliament form a new state by uniting two or more states or parts of states. So exactly 1 is correct.

questions.q:
Consider the following statements about the Punjab and Himachal changes:

1. The union territory of Himachal Pradesh was elevated to the status of a state in 1971, as the 18th state.
2. The State of Himachal Pradesh Act (1970) elevated the union territory of Himachal Pradesh to a state.
3. Chandigarh was made a union territory as well as a common capital for Punjab and Haryana.

How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.e: Statement 1 is correct: the union territory of Himachal Pradesh became a state in 1971, as the 18th state. Statement 2 is correct: the State of Himachal Pradesh Act (1970) elevated it. Statement 3 is correct: under the Punjab Reorganisation Act (1966) Chandigarh was made a union territory as well as a common capital for Punjab and Haryana. So exactly 3 are correct.
w: 'Only two' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'Only one' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
'None' miscounts: exactly 3 are correct (statements 1, 2, 3).
